children: Dan Towriss, the head of Mark Walter's insurance companies, told the Department of Justice that he wasn't aware that the business had loaned more than $20B to Walter's other businesses, according to a media report on Tuesday.

The head of Delaware Life Insurance Co. and Clear Spring Life and Annuity Co. provided the statements in a voluntary interview with federal prosecutors in late August, Bloomberg News reported, citing two people with knowledge of the matter. Another person said he recently made similar to Delaware state regulators.

The remarks raise the question of how Walter, the owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers, was able to borrow from his insurers without having the insurance units report them to state regulators, as required. The two insurance companies eventually disclosed the loans in a June filing. Meanwhile, the U.S. Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission have opened investigations into the loans.

Insurers are legally required to disclose to regulators which of their investments involve affiliates — businesses that are controlled by the same owner as the insurer. Towriss said he was unaware that the ultimate recipients of the loans were associated with Walter, the people told  Bloomberg.

Bloomberg had previously reported that many of the loans being investigated went to third-party companies controlled by people with ties to Walter. From those firms, the money was loaned to other businesses controlled by Walter.

title: Walter's insurance CEO said he was unaware of loans to other Walter businesses - report
